newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00-2.00 cents lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00-2.00 cents lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 to 2.00 cents lower Tuesday although a slightly smaller-than-expected rise in U.S. consumer coffee stocks in May is expected to underpin prices, traders said.

Green Coffee Association of New York reported after the Monday's close that supplies of green coffee stowed in U.S. warehouses rose in May by 122,000 60-kg bags, to 1,977,000 bags. Most industry participants had expected a build of some 150,000-250,000 bags in May.
"It is a little bullish," said one trader, "but not too much."

Monday, New York arabica futures ended mixed after a bout of speculative shortcovering cut early losses. September closed down 1.15 cents at 181.60 cents a lb after ranging from 182.00 to 175.00. Spot July rose 0.80 cent to 196.50, while the back months finished up 1.00 to down 1.30.
The July/September switch widened to 14.90 cents at the close, from 12.95 on Friday.
Technically, traders said the spot July contract would run into support at 192.00, then 188.00. On the upside, 200.00 was seen as resistance.

Fundamentally, German statistician F.O. Licht said on Tuesday that world coffee production is forecast to rise to a revised 99 million bags in 1996/97, up from it previous estimate of 97.7 million and 87.88 million in 1995/96.
The upward revision reflects higher robusta output, Licht said. The estimate for robusta coffee was raised by 1.2 million bags to 33.47 million, while arabicas was reduced by 42,000 bags.

In its latest estimate of the world coffee balance, Licht said exports could reach 77.78 million bags from 73.35 million in 1995/96, while global consumption (including the 25 million bags consumed in producing countries) could total 99.5 million.

On the weather front, no damaging cold is expected this week in Brazil's coffee belt, although recent wet weather was of concern because of the impact on harvesting, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Tuesday.
After Monday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 3,520 bags as of June 13, to 48,050 bags. There were 1,038 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
London robusta futures were broadly higher early Tuesday, in light switch-dominated trading. At the midday break, LIFFE September rose $47 to $1,825 and spot July was $44 higher, at $1,795.
